The test image shows tomato plants in a commercial field (black plastic mulch). The center plants are completely collapsed/wilted — drooping severely at or near the soil line — while surrounding plants remain healthy. This is a whole-plant symptom, pointing to vascular or soil-line diseases.

Top candidates: Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Blight, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt, Verticillium_Wilt.

Now viewing one reference image from each of the 4 candidates:

The Southern_Bacterial_Wilt reference (Bugwood_15.jpg, #5593860) is a near-perfect visual match to the test image (#5593858) — same black plastic mulch, same sandy field, same complete plant collapse pattern, and consecutive Bugwood image numbers suggesting the same photoset. Let me use my 4th view on Verticillium_Wilt to rule it out.

Verticillium_Wilt shows leaf-level V-shaped necrotic lesions — clearly not matching the whole-plant collapse in the test image.

**Summary of evidence:**
- Test image: Complete collapse of 2 center plants on black plastic mulch, sandy field, neighboring plants healthy
- Bacterial_Wilt reference: Similar wilt but on staked/wire-trained vines, less severe collapse
- Southern_Blight reference: Lower-leaf wilt, plants still upright with fruit
- **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt reference (Bugwood_15, #5593860): Near-identical match** — same black mulch, same sandy/arid setting, same complete drooping collapse, and Bugwood numbers are consecutive (test = 5593858, reference = 5593860), confirming same documentation photoset
- Verticillium_Wilt: Leaf-level symptom only, no match
